Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Aishwarya Pratap Singh,Amit Kumar Malviya Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
Heard Sri Aishwarya Pratap Singh and Sri Amit Kumar Malviya, learned counsels for the applicant and Sri Ravi Kant Kushwaha, learned AGA for the State.

The instant bail application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No.
328 of 2021, under Sections 419, 420, 467, 468, 471 IPC, Police Station Puramufti, District Prayagraj during pendency of the trial.

FIR of the present case was lodged on 03.10.2021 and according to the FIR, applicant along with co-accused Chhedilal Prajapati got executed a fake sale deed in their favour in the year 2016 from one Maika Devi and thereafter he executed a sale deed of the property in favour of the informant and thus both applicant and co-accused Chhedilal Prajapati duped the informant.

Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that entire allegation made against the applicant is totally false and baseless and in fact applicant and co-accused Chhedilal Prajapati got executed a sale deed from one Maika Devi in the year 2014 and they did not commit any fraud and in the year 2016 applicant and co-accused Chhedilal Prajapati executed a sale deed of the property in favour of the informant and two others but at the time of execution of the sale deed and its registry entire Ashok Kumar Ojha vs State Of U.P. on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80331777/
1 consideration was not paid and out of Rs. 30 Lakhs only Rs. 20 Lakhs were paid and in spite of repeated demand made by the applicant, informant did not pay Rs. 10 Lakhs and instead of making payment of Rs. 10 Lakhs he lodged FIR of the present case on 03.10.2021.

sentences.text: He further submitted surprisingly during investigation, Investigation Officer neither recorded the statement of Maika Devi, the owner of the property, who executed sale deed in favour of applicant and co-accused Chhedilal Prajapati in the year 2014 nor statement of two other purchasers were recorded, who purchased the land from the applicant and co-accused Chhedilal Prajapati in the year 2016 along with informant.

He next submits that even from the allegation it appears that informant is having right to file civil suit for cancellation of the sale deed dated 22.01.2016, which was executed by the applicant and co-accused in his favour.

He next submitted that although applicant is having criminal history of six other cases but he has explained his criminal history in paragraph 46 of the affidavit filed in support of present application.

Applicant in the present matter is in jail since 01.02.2022 i.e.
for last about more than a year.

He next submitted that co-accused Chhedilal Prajapati has been released on anticipatory bail by the co-ordinate Bench of this Court vide order dated 18.11.2022 passed in Criminal Misc. Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. 10845 of 2022.
Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail but could not dispute the argument on facts advanced by learned counsel for the applicant.
I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

Although, as per allegation made in the FIR applicant along with co-accused Chhedilal Prajapati executed a sale deed in favour of informant and two others in the year 2016 of the property, which they purchased from one Maika Devi in the year 2014, but subsequently it was revealed to the informant that the sale deed which alleged to have been executed by Maika Devi in favour of applicant and co-accused was fake one but from the perusal of the record, it appears that during investigation, Investigating Officer neither recorded the statement of Maika Devi nor recorded the statement of two other persons, who were also purchasers of the property in question along with informant and this fact has not been disputed by learned AGA.
Further, co-accused Chhedilal Prajapati has been enlarged on anticipatory bail by the co-ordinate Bench of this Court vide order dated 18.11.2022 and further applicant in the present matter is in jail since 01.02.2022 i.e. for last about more than a year, therefore, in view of this Court, it is a fit case to release the applicant on bail.
In the light of discussions made above, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

Let the applicant - Ashok Kumar Ojha be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.

In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.
